segments.text: This video

will show us how we can
adjust our grid preferences
within Altium Designer.

The schematic editor is based
on the principle of working with the grid,

which is present in the background
of the schematic sheet.

All placed objects, of any type,
are placed at the intersection point

of the grid lines
with a certain distance.

Altium Designer allows us
to configure visible grids

for ease of
document navigation,

and snap grids for precise
component placement and wiring.

Let's explore how we can adjust
our grid preferences and appearance.

We’ll open
our system preferences

and expand
the Schematic branch.
Then open the grids page.

Within the
grid preferences,

we can modify
the color of the grid.

For example,
let's change the grid color to red.
Further,

we can change the grid
from lines to dots, as shown.

We’ll change the Grid Options
back to White,
and Lines.
Below the grid options,

we can find
grid presets

for both imperial
and metric units.

These presets include
coarse and fine grids

that we can select
for different snap grid,
snap distance,

and visible grid
settings.

For example,
if we select Course (3 settings),

we can see this selects
50 mil, 100 mil,

and 200 mil selectable grids
for our schematics.

We’ll press OK
to close the preferences dialog.

With our Course (3 settings)
Grid Preset selected

we can press
the ‘G’ key

to switch between
the 50 mil,

100 mil,
and 200 mil grids

as shown in the status bar
near the bottom of the window.

The visible grid in the background
of the schematic sheet

also changes to match
the grid size setting.

Finally, don't forget,
if you ever get stuck within Altium,

you can press
the ‘F1’ key

which will provide access
to information

for any resource
that is currently under the cursor.
In this video,

we explored grid preferences
within Altium Designer.

title: Altium Training - Schematic Preferences: Grid Preferences
